_comment: OHAO golden-image regression corpus. Run from repo root.
_what_this_gate_actually_is: Read this before trusting a green run, and before loosening anything.
These scenes are Monte Carlo path traces. The renderer is deterministic for
a fixed sampler and a fixed build -- two runs are byte-identical -- so this
corpus is, in practice, a HASH of an unchanged sampler with enough slack for
the GPU floating-point floor. It is not a tolerance gate in the sense of
'the image is still about right', and it cannot be made into one by raising
the sample count. Measured on cornell_box against a 1024 spp reference:
16 spp is max_abs 88 / rmse 10.8, 64 spp is 47 / 6.9, 256 spp is 34 / 4.1.
Noise falls as 1/sqrt(N), so a max_abs 4 tolerance is out of reach at any
sample count anyone will wait for.
WHAT IT CATCHES: a changed shader, a changed material, a broken pass, a
missing asset -- anything that moves pixels while the sample sequence stays
put. That is the common case and the gate is genuinely good at it.
WHAT IT CANNOT DISTINGUISH: a real regression from any change that perturbs
the sample SEQUENCE (a new sampler dimension, a reordered bounce, a changed
seed). Both reshuffle every pixel by the noise magnitude. When you change
sampling, this corpus will go red and it cannot tell you whether you also
broke something. Verify that case by eye or with a converged render.
max_abs_diff 4 is sized for the cross-session GPU floor, not for noise. The
same SPIR-V on the same machine has been measured drifting 3 channels of
6.2M by 1 LSB between sessions; 4 covers that with margin.
_growing: Denoiser OFF on every scene: we pin raw deterministic beauty. A denoiser is a large, version-dependent, non-linear prior, and pinning its output pins the denoiser rather than the renderer.
Grow this list as features land -- every fixed bug should add a scene so it cannot silently regress. A scene costs one entry here and a few seconds a run.

A scene must load only TRACKED assets, or it is not a gate on a fresh clone. Not a style rule: the scene this replaced pointed at a file nobody had, and its empty render was reported as a pixel regression for two months.
_regenerating: It overwrites without comparing, so it cannot tell an intentional refresh
from laundering a regression. Look at what drifted FIRST. The goldens these
replaced were 78 renderer commits stale and nobody knew, because the harness
could not run at all on a multi-config generator.

scenes.name: cornell_box
scenes._note: Builds its scene in code and loads no asset, so it runs on a bare clone.

scenes.name: damaged_helmet
scenes._note: Replaces metal_rough_spheres, whose MetalRoughSpheres.glb was never in the repository. model_viewer used to exit 0 after a failed load and render an empty frame, so that scene reported a large pixel difference for two months instead of a missing file. DamagedHelmet.glb IS tracked (3.7 MB) and covers the same ground: a metal/rough glTF under an HDRI.
